title: Finite-stage duality under the site comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. The finite coefficient stage is $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism].

Use $D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for the bounded complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for its full subcategory with Tor amplitude in some finite interval: for some integers $a\le b$ and every degree-zero module sheaf $N$, $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^L N)=0$ for $r\notin[a,b]$ [lem-sf-flat-model]. On the pro-etale site use [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Internal Hom is the derived sheaf Hom of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on each site.

For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical evaluation-defined map
$$
\beta_{K,M}:\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$
is an isomorphism. Let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism. Put $\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}=a_X^{\times}A$, where $a_X^{\times}$ is the etale compact-support right adjoint, and put $\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}=Ra_X^!A$, where $Ra_X^!$ is its comparison-class transport [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\nu_X^*\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}\cong\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}.
$$
Writing $D_{X,\tau}K=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_{X,\tau})$ for $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$, these comparisons identify the evaluation pairings $D_{X,\tau}K\otimes_A^LK\to\omega_{X,\tau}$ and their transposes $K\to D_{X,\tau}D_{X,\tau}K$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. In particular the finite-stage Verdier duality on $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ is transported from etale Verdier duality. No ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint on arbitrary complexes is assumed.

proof.text:
The comparison inverse image is exact and identifies the two constant coefficient rings by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. The tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to this flat ringed-site morphism, therefore makes $
u^*$ a strong monoidal functor on the derived categories. Define $ eta_{K,M}$ by transposing
$$

u^*R\mathcal Hom(K,M)\otimes^L
u^*K\cong
u^*(R\mathcal Hom(K,M)\otimes^LK)\xrightarrow{
u^*\mathrm{ev}}
u^*M.
$$
The tensor-Hom adjunction used here is obtained as follows on either ringed site. Choose K-flat representatives of the two tensor arguments by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of the target, whose existence is part of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The functorial complex isomorphism of [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] identifies $\mathcal Hom^ ullet(Q,\mathcal Hom^ ullet(P,I))$ with $\mathcal Hom^ ullet(\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes P),I)$. The inner Hom is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], so taking zeroth derived global sections and using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,R\mathcal Hom(P,I))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q\otimes^LP,I)$. Its evaluation is the transpose of the identity, and at the dualizing target this is the pairing of [lem-weil-duality-pairing]. This formula specifies the map to be checked, rather than just an unspecified isomorphism. Inverse-image comparison with scheme pullback follows by composing the two inverse-image adjunctions: both compositions are left adjoint to the same direct-image composition, as seen by evaluating at the fibre product. Thus open restriction commutes with comparison, including its units and counits.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: exact comparison and open restrictions; evaluation convention in the final paragraph

proof.text:
Here is the closed exceptional comparison required by the stratum calculation. For $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with open complement $j$ and bounded constructible etale $M$, apply exact $
u_T^*$ to the etale triangle of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. The direct-image comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] identifies its outside direct images with $i_*
u_Z^*Ri_{\mathrm{et}}^!M$ and $Rj_{\mathrm{proet},*}j^*
u_T^*M$. This theorem applies to $j$ and $i$: all schemes here are Noetherian of finite type, hence the complementary open is quasi-compact and both morphisms are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its bounded-below condition holds for $Ri^!M$, because the etale support triangle expresses $i_*Ri^!M$ as the fibre of a map between bounded-below objects and etale $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-kun-04ca] (the abelian counit is coefficient-linear, so the same inverse is a module map). Compare this with [lem-exc-proetale-support-triangle]. Both arrows from the middle term are the restriction unit, so their fibres are identified by the induced map of mapping-cone models. The exactness and full faithfulness in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact] and [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] give
$$
u_Z^*Ri_{\mathrm{et}}^!M\cong Ri_{\mathrm{proet}}^!
u_T^*M.$$
Indeed $i_*$ preserves K-injectives since its exact left adjoint is $i^*$, and its derived counit is the termwise sheaf counit; hence its derived full faithfulness follows too. Open exceptional restriction is ordinary restriction; factoring a locally closed immersion $s$ as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion and composing the adjunction bijections gives the same comparison for $Rs^!$. On etale-origin inputs this is the transported functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]: the unit isomorphism $\mathrm{id}\cong R
u_*
u^*$ of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies its formula with $
u_S^*s^{	imes}$. The adjunction comparison in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] fixes its counits. Finally [thm-sf-preservation-class] makes this transported value bounded constructible; the equivalence [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and full faithfulness on $D^+$ then imply that $N=Rs_{\mathrm{et}}^!M$ itself is bounded constructible. Thus the second-variable hypothesis needed below is verified; no finite-Tor hypothesis on $M$ or $N$ was introduced.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: compare the closed-support triangles; third paragraph: locally closed exceptional restriction

proof.text:
We make the generator reduction explicit without borrowing a stratification from the proof of another node. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], $
u_X^*$ is an equivalence on bounded constructible finite-Tor objects. Apply the generation statement of [lem-trf-devissage-generation] on the pro-etale side. Its generators have the form $g_*j_!L$, where $j:S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ is open, $g:\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ is closed, and $L$ is lisse with finite flat stalks. The lisse descent statement [lem-sf-proetale-locally-constant-origin] supplies a lisse etale $L_0$ with $
u_S^*L_0\cong L$. It has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by the converse in [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]: a locally constant sheaf with flat stalks is locally a constant flat module, so tensoring it is exact. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] and [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image],
$$
u_X^*(Rg_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et},!}L_0)\cong Rg_{\mathrm{proet},*}j_{\mathrm{proet},!}L.$$
All these objects are bounded constructible, and the equivalence lifts the finite cones, shifts and retract diagrams exhibiting generation. Hence the etale $D^b_{ctf}$ is generated thickly by these etale objects $Rs_!L_0$. This uses the statements of the generation and lisse-descent nodes, not their internal proofs.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: finite stratification and reduction to extensions from site-perfect strata

proof.text: For fixed $M$ the property that $\beta_{K,M}$ is an isomorphism is thick in $K$. On the etale side exactness in the first variable is [lem-sf-hom-triangulated]. On the pro-etale side this is the following explicit calculation with [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [def-pur-hom-complex]: for a map $u:K_1\to K_2$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of the second variable, $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Cone}(u),I)$ is the shifted cone of $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K_2,I)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K_1,I)$, with the differential $d(f)=d_I f-(-1)^{|f|}f d_K$. This is checked on the two cone summands, and descends to the derived category because the chosen internal Hom does. Exact $\nu^*$ carries cone triangles to triangles, and the transpose formula in step 1 is natural, so these are morphisms of triangles. If two components are isomorphisms, the long exact cohomology sequences give the third by the five lemma. Shifts and finite sums are preserved. If $K$ is a retract of $K'$ with inclusion $u$ and projection $v$, an inverse for its component is $F(u)\beta_{K',M}^{-1}G(v)$, where $F,G$ are the two contravariant functors; the two inverse identities follow from naturality and $vu=1$. It therefore suffices to check the generators from step 3.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: triangulated internal Hom and induction through the triangles

proof.text: For a generator $Rs_!L_0$, set $N=Rs_{\mathrm{et}}^!M$, bounded constructible by step 2. The ring $A$ is finite and local by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], hence Noetherian (an ascending chain of ideals is an ascending chain of subsets of a finite set). On an etale cover trivializing $L_0$ its module value is a finite flat $A$-module. Apply [lem-weil-bounded-finite-tor-perfect] to that module in degree zero with interval $[0,0]$: it is finite projective, and therefore finite free because $A$ is local. Thus $L_0$ is etale-locally $A^{\oplus r}[0]$, a site-perfect object. Apply [lem-sf-hom-comparison-finite-free] on each such cover member to this first variable and $N$; it gives $\beta_{L_0,N}$ there. Here is why this local check suffices. Restriction of a K-injective remains K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], and the Hom-complex formula of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] restricts termwise to the slice site, so restriction of $R\mathcal Hom$ is the internal Hom of the restricted inputs. The pro-etale slice is the small pro-etale site of the cover member by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]; the etale slice has the same description by composing etale maps. The evaluation formula in step 1 restricts to the displayed local comparison. The etale covering is also a pro-etale covering, and [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative](1) detects its being an isomorphism. Therefore $\beta_{L_0,N}$ is an isomorphism on $S$.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: comparison for a site-perfect first variable, with its locality justification

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-stratum-ambient-hom] on both sites. Under its canonical tensor-adjunction identifications, the comparison for a generator is the composite
$$
\nu_X^*Rs_{\mathrm{et},*}R\mathcal Hom(L_0,N)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_{\mathrm{proet},*}\nu_S^*R\mathcal Hom(L_0,N)
\xrightarrow{Rs_*\beta_{L_0,N}}Rs_{\mathrm{proet},*}R\mathcal Hom(\nu_S^*L_0,\nu_S^*N)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_{\mathrm{proet},*}R\mathcal Hom(\nu_S^*L_0,Rs_{\mathrm{proet}}^!\nu_X^*M).
$$
The first arrow is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], the second is step 5, and the last is step 2. The first arrow is applicable: $s$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $R\mathcal Hom(L_0,N)$ is bounded below because locally it is the finite sum $N^{\oplus r}$. To check that this composite is the specified $\beta_{Rs_!L_0,M}$, uncurry it. The stratum-adjunction identity is obtained by evaluating on $S$ and applying the counit $Rs_!Rs^!M\to M$. Step 2 identifies that counit under comparison, step 5 identifies evaluation, and the direct-image comparison is the adjunction mate of the commuting pullbacks. Thus uncurrying the displayed composite gives exactly $\nu_X^*\mathrm{ev}$ from step 1; injectivity of the tensor-Hom adjunction gives equality of the maps. Every arrow is invertible, so the generator comparison is invertible. Step 4 and generation prove $\beta_{K,M}$ for all stated inputs.

source.place: Proof, second and third paragraphs: stratum internal Hom identity and assembly of the canonical comparison

proof.text:
Put $a=a_X$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. By the transported exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image],
$$
\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}=
u_X^*a^{	imes}R
u_{s,*}A_{s,\mathrm{proet}}.
$$
Exact comparison identifies $A_{s,\mathrm{proet}}=
u_s^*A_{s,\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], and the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies $R
u_{s,*}
u_s^*A$ with $A$. Substituting gives the required canonical $w:
u_X^*\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$. This single global formula provides the overlap compatibility that the imported local-embedding argument left implicit. The preservation statement [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata], applied to the unit $A_X$ of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$, shows that $\omega_{X,\mathrm{et}}=D_{X,\mathrm{et}}A_X$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude; it also shows the same for $D_{X,\mathrm{et}}K$ when $K$ is finite-Tor constructible. These are precisely its stated conclusions, rather than a stratification borrowed from its proof.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: dualizing-object comparison; global version using the current exceptional-inverse-image convention

proof.text:
Write $F=\nu_X^*$, $D=D_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ and $D'=D_{X,\mathrm{proet}}$. Steps 6 and 7 define $c_K:FDK\xrightarrow{\sim}D'FK$ by $\beta_{K,\omega}$ followed by $R\mathcal Hom(FK,w)$. Its defining equation is
$$
\mathrm{ev}'_{FK}\circ(c_K\otimes1)=w\circ F(\mathrm{ev}_K)
$$
under the monoidal identification of step 1. This proves evaluation compatibility. The construction of [lem-weil-duality-pairing] defines $\delta_K$ by transposing $\mathrm{ev}_K$ with the tensor factors interchanged. Since $DK$ is finite-Tor constructible by step 7, step 6 also applies to it. The resulting comparison of double duals is
$$
FDDK\xrightarrow{c_{DK}}D'FDK\xrightarrow{D'(c_K^{-1})}D'D'FK.
$$
Uncurrying its composite with $F\delta_K$ gives the factor-interchanged evaluation above: use the evaluation equation for $K$ and $DK$, and naturality of evaluation for $c_K^{-1}$. It is the same transpose that defines $\delta'_{FK}$, so
$$\delta'_{FK}=D'(c_K^{-1})\circ c_{DK}\circ F(\delta_K).$$
These equations explicitly identify the double-dual maps. Finally [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] give an equivalence on the finite-Tor bounded constructible categories; $c$ identifies their duality functors. The etale biduality theorem [thm-weil-etale-geometric-biduality] then makes the displayed pro-etale double-dual map invertible and transports the etale anti-equivalence. This final application uses the already separate etale theorem, which has no dependency on the present site-comparison lemma.

source.place: Proof, final paragraph: evaluation, double-dual maps, and transport of finite-stage Verdier duality
